title: Growing without soil
subtitle: A classroom hydroponics project
intro: How do you turn a wooden frame, a few pipes, and a question into a living system? In science, we’re designing and building a hydroponic garden—and making sense of every choice along the way.
question: How can we build a system that reliably grows plants in our classroom, and support our choices with scientific evidence?
now: The frame, growing channels, and lights are in place. Our focus is the water system: splitting one pump line into four upper channels, connecting each to its own lower channel, and bringing the four returns back together.
next: Finish the connections, test for leaks and drainage, and observe how evenly water reaches all four routes. Planting and nutrient monitoring come after the water system is working.
modelNote: A photo-informed study of our build. Proportions, planting holes, slopes, and fitting positions are illustrative; exact measurements are still to come. The tubing shows the intended route, not a tested installation.

phases.title: Start with a question
phases.description: Investigate food, land use, and what plants need. Identify the jobs our system must do: provide structure, light, water, nutrients, drainage, and monitoring.
phases.evidence: Notice-and-wonder observations and explanations of plant needs.

phases.title: Design & build
phases.description: Work within limits of space, time, and materials. Assemble the structure, plan connections, and use patterns to understand how tees create branches.
phases.evidence: Build sketches, fitting counts, and reasons for design choices.

phases.title: Follow the water
phases.description: Connect the pump, channels, and return. Investigate gravity, height, flow, and the effect of changing one part of the system.
phases.evidence: Leak checks, observations, flow measurements, and revisions.

phases.title: Support living plants
phases.description: Germinate and transplant lettuce. Connect light and photosynthesis to plant growth, and investigate nutrients, pH, and water conditions.
phases.evidence: Plant observations, growth records, and water measurements.

phases.title: Test, improve & explain
phases.description: Use observations to diagnose problems, compare changes, and consider resource use. Explain how the whole system works using claims and evidence.
phases.evidence: A design defense, reflection, and a harvest celebration when the plants are ready.

lessons.title: How much land does food take?
lessons.description: Connect food choices to the space needed to grow food.

lessons.title: The six missing pieces
lessons.description: Identify plant needs and the jobs a hydroponic system has to do.

lessons.title: Vote and get ready
lessons.description: Name criteria, constraints, and the first steps of a build.

lessons.title: How many tees do we need?
lessons.description: Build branching models and use a pattern to explain fitting counts.
